samples.summary: IMAGE_METADATA_RE's unbounded lazy span backtracks quadratically, reintroducing the per-keystroke main-thread freeze MAX_FENCE_CHARS/MAX_STRIP_PASSES were added to bound
samples.evidence: `const IMAGE_METADATA_RE = /@\s*\{[\s\S]*?["']?img["']?\s*:/i` (line 351). `[\s\S]*?` is unanchored and unbounded, so for a source containing many `@{` occurrences and no `img:`, the engine retries the lazy span from every `@{` start position, each scan running to end of input: a 50 000-char body of `@{@{@{…` is ~25 000 starts × ~50 000 chars ≈ 1.2e9 steps. `prepareFenceSource()` runs on the fresh source of every keystroke (the render cache is keyed by exact source, so a typing user never hits it), so this is a stored main-thread stall of exactly the kind MAX_FENCE_CHARS/MAX_STRIP_PASSES were introduced to prevent — the length cap alone does not bound superlinear work.

samples.summary: IMAGE_METADATA_RE matches across the whole fence body and matches `img` without a word boundary, refusing legitimate diagrams
samples.evidence: Because `[\s\S]*?` is not limited to the metadata block, ANY `@{ … }` shape/edge metadata anywhere in the source combined with the substring `img:` anywhere later (including inside a word, e.g. `B["myimg: none"]` — the leading `["']?` is optional and there is no `\b` before `img`) refuses the whole diagram with "image shapes are not allowed". The doc comment concedes a false positive on a label that says `img:`, but the actual span is the entire document, not the block, which is broader than described and will hit real mermaid 11 sources that use `e1@{ animate: true }` plus prose containing `img:`.

samples.summary: FETCH_TAG_RE's "a literal `<` is all an HTML parser can turn into an element" assumption ignores mermaid's own `#NN;`/`#quot;` entity decoding
samples.evidence: `FETCH_TAG_RE` (line 339) matches only a literal `<`, and the SECURITY note asserts "Entity-encoding is not a way around it: an HTML parser turns `<img>` into text, not an element" (lines 90-91). That is true of HTML entities, but mermaid supports its own escape syntax (`#quot;`, `#35;`, decimal `#NN;`) and decodes it (`common.decodeEntities`, `/#\w+;/`) while building labels — so `#60;img src=https://evil.example/b.png#62;` carries no literal `<` past this guard and can be reassembled inside the label paths that still emit a foreignObject (sequence/kanban/venn/architecture), which the note itself says are sanitized with DOMPurify's DEFAULT allowlist that permits ``. I could not verify against the installed engine (node_modules is absent in this tree), hence low confidence, but the guard's stated invariant does not hold for mermaid's non-HTML entity spelling.

For input with many `@{` starts and no `img:`, every `@{` position re-scans to end of input, giving ~O(n^2/4) steps (~6e8 for a 50k-char `@{@{@{...` body) since JS regex does no memoization. finding.summary: Top-level `htmlLabels: false` may not actually turn off HTML labels — mermaid resolves it with `||` against the per-diagram default `true`
finding.evidence: mermaid.ts:470-477 asserts "the engine resolves labels through `config.htmlLabels ?? config.flowchart?.htmlLabels ?? true`". In mermaid 11 the label helper (rendering-util/rendering-elements/shapes/util.ts `labelHelper`, and createLabel.js) reads `node.useHtmlLabels || getConfig()?.htmlLabels || getConfig()?.flowchart?.htmlLabels` — a logical OR, not `??`. With OR, a top-level `false` is falsy and falls straight through to `flowchart.htmlLabels`, whose schema default is `true`, so the foreignObject label subtree is still built and the `` in a label is still fetched during layout. Additionally, other diagram types read their own namespaced keys (`class.htmlLabels`, `state.htmlLabels`, mindmap/er label paths) which the top-level key does not reach at all, so even under the `??` reading the mitigation is only partial. If either holds, the whole change is a no-op for the behavior it claims to fix. mermaid is not installed in this working tree so I could not read the installed 11.16.0 source to confirm; the config would need `flowchart: { htmlLabels: false }` (and the equivalent per-diagram keys) in addition to the root key.

verdict.reason: The code is not as described. The finding's premise is that only the root `htmlLabels: false` is set, so an `||`-based resolver would fall through to `flowchart.htmlLabels`'s default `true`; its prescribed fix is to also set `flowchart: { htmlLabels: false }`. That fix is already in the tree: `mermaid.ts:636-638` sets `htmlLabels: false`, `flowchart: { htmlLabels: false }` AND `class: { htmlLabels: false }`, so every term of the `node.useHtmlLabels || config.htmlLabels || config.flowchart?.htmlLabels` chain is false and the result is `false` under either the `??` or `||` reading. The comment the finding quotes as asserting `??` (claimed at mermaid.ts:470-477, which is actually `decodeCssEscapes`) is at mermaid.ts:619-630 and explicitly says the opposite: the sections are pinned precisely because some renderers read `flowchart.htmlLabels` directly, "so the answer is `false` under either reading rather than resting on which one a given release happens to use". The residual claim (other diagram types read their own namespaced keys) is also unreachable for the behavior it targets: `prepareFenceSource()` refuses the fence before the engine is invoked — FETCH_TAG_RE (mermaid.ts:338-339, checked at :390) rejects any `` in the source, IMAGE_METADATA_RE (:351/:393) rejects `img:` shape metadata, and hasCssFetch (:396) rejects external CSS url()/@import — so an `` in an HTML-label diagram type (sequence/venn/kanban) never reaches layout (asserted at preview.test.ts:775-792). Finally, preview.test.ts:708-732 runs the production config through REAL mermaid and asserts the engine's own serialized output has no `foreignObject`, with a control at :734-748 showing the same source does emit one at the engine's default — which would fail if the mitigation collapsed to `true` as claimed. The change is therefore not a no-op.

finding.summary: Fixpoint strip loop is quadratic in fence length on untrusted input, with no size bound before it runs — a hostile note can hang the reader's tab
finding.evidence:
stripConfigDirectives() now loops until a fixpoint (lines 250-255). Each iteration runs an unanchored global `DIRECTIVE_RE` scan plus a full string copy over the whole remaining source, while `FRONTMATTER_RE` removes at most ONE leading block per iteration. A source of stacked ~10-byte `---
x
---
` blocks therefore costs O(n²/10): the docstring's own numbers (29 ms at 50 kB) only hold because it assumes mermaid's `maxTextSize` default bounds the input, but `maxTextSize` is enforced inside `mermaid.render()` (line 504) — strictly AFTER stripConfigDirectives() has already run on the raw fence body, which nothing in preview.ts or mermaid.ts caps. A 1 MB fence of stacked blocks is ~100k iterations over ~500 kB average, i.e. tens of GB of scanning/copying on the main thread, synchronously inside renderPass. Cross-carrier promotion (directive+frontmatter alternation) reaches the same iteration count. A cheap fix: bail out (or fall back to leaving the source intact / erroring the block) past a small iteration count or an input-length cap, since the docstring itself notes only a hostile fence stacks more than one carrier.

verdict.reason: The described code does not exist in this repository. `stripConfigDirectives()` (mermaid.ts:317-325) does NOT loop to a fixpoint: it runs a bounded `for (let pass = 0; pass < MAX_STRIP_PASSES; pass++)` with `MAX_STRIP_PASSES = 8` (mermaid.ts:278) and returns `null` (mermaid.ts:324) if the source is still changing after the last pass, which the caller turns into a refusal message (mermaid.ts:400-402). The claim that "nothing caps" the input is also false: the sole production caller `prepareFenceSource()` enforces `if (source.length > MAX_FENCE_CHARS) return { error }` at mermaid.ts:385-389 with `MAX_FENCE_CHARS = 50_000` (mermaid.ts:272) BEFORE invoking the strip at mermaid.ts:399, and mermaid.ts:266-272 documents that this exists precisely because mermaid's own `maxTextSize` is enforced later inside `render()`. A repo-wide grep of `.ts/.tsx/.js` shows the only production call sites are mermaid.ts:399 (strip, post-cap) and mermaid.ts:663 (`prepareFenceSource` in renderPass); no path reaches the loop with an uncapped body. Worst-case work is 50 kB x 8 passes, not quadratic in an unbounded body. The reviewer's suggested fix (iteration bound + length cap + error fallback) is already implemented verbatim.
